metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to underpredict sharp downward moves; adjust forecast downward by 2–5% for 1–3 day horizons.
- After a spike in price (e.g., >30% from prior peak), model often overreacts and overshoots — cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak for 1–2 day horizons.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-period, model lags in upward correction — add 1–3% upward bias in next 3–5 day forecast.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price near 30-day moving average, model tends to overpredict divergence — reduce forecast by 1–3% for 5–7 day horizons.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently underestimates volatility in high-sentiment periods — increase forecast range by 10–20% if sentiment > 0.5 for 3+ consecutive days.
- If sentiment is negative and price is trending upward, model often fails to recognize reversal — reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for 3–7 day horizons.
